# Rendering and Layout

## Layout
- `SizeConstraint`: `Fixed(n)`, `Flex(weight)`, `Auto`, and `Min`/`Max` wrappers. Widgets default to `Flex(1)` on both axes unless they have a natural size (`Checkbox` height is `Fixed(1)`; `TextBlock` and `Spinner` default to `Auto` since 0.4.0).
- [`LayoutSolver.ResolveSizes()`](mex://method:82f16e943049535fbab20d6eea3405c9) is the single place sizes are computed, called by both `LayoutEngine` (which builds the `ResolvedLayout` that focus and hit-testing read) and `Container.Render` (which places children). Pass 1 gives fixed/measured children their size and parks flex children; pass 2 splits leftover space by weight, the rounding remainder going to the last flex child. Fixed children that overflow a container with no flex and nothing measured throw `LayoutConstraintException`; measured overflow is scaled back instead.
- `Auto` measures only when the widget implements `IMeasurable` — `Measure(availableWidth, availableHeight)` runs during layout, so it must be pure, cheap, and never ask for more than offered. Without `IMeasurable`, `Auto` behaves as flex weight 1. [`LayoutSolver.DesiredSize()`](mex://method:46a3e20938a24b61aed2d2beb0f98b68) is the helper containers use to report their own desired size from their children.
- Margin and padding come from `Style` and are enforced by the solver (`includeMargins`), not by widgets.

## Renderer
- [`Renderer.RenderIfDirty()`](mex://method:f15e3fea0df2ea590eaf89969a744ebf) re-renders only when dirty, resized, or the theme changed. It reuses one of two `ResolvedLayout` buffers (`NextLayoutBuffer`), resets a single long-lived `RenderContext`, calls `root.Render(ctx)`, builds the ANSI frame, and flushes.
- The frame is a cell-level diff against the previous buffer: untouched cells are not re-emitted. `Invalidate()` drops the previous buffer to force a full redraw (resize does this).
- The widget render cache (`IRenderContext.TryReuseWidget`, implemented in `RenderContext` and forwarded by `SubRenderContext`) lets an unchanged widget reuse its previously rendered cells. Because a cache miss still produces identical pixels, cache regressions are invisible to snapshot tests — `WidgetCacheTests` counts hits directly.
- `TryGetLastFrame` exposes the last `(root, layout)` for hit-testing; callers must hold `App._renderLock` because the next frame reclaims that layout buffer.

## Raw escape payloads (images)
- A widget emits pixel graphics by passing an `IRawEscapePayload` to `IRenderContext.WriteRawEscape`; it bypasses the cell buffer. `ImageWidget` + `RgbaImageData` use `KittyProtocol` where supported and fall back to half-block cells with 24-bit colour elsewhere.
- Payloads are tracked across frames by `ContentHash`, not region. A hash seen last frame is re-positioned via [`Place()`](mex://method:e0bb5b7e46383cb1827217f3f6982d61) (defaults to `Encode`) instead of re-uploaded; a new hash is sent through `Encode`. Change the hash when content changes. `Renderer.BuildRawCleanup` deletes placed graphics on exit.
- `Cmd.Preload(payload)` uploads ahead of first appearance via `IRawEscapePayload.Transmit` (default null = no separate step). `RenderContext` keeps a held-hash set: first appearance of a held hash goes through `Place()`, the entry is then consumed; dropped on resize. `App.DispatchCmd` handles a sync `PreloadMsg` immediately so the upload beats the frame.
- Pixel-path benchmarks: `./bench.sh -f '*Pixel*'` (shelf frame kinds in/out of tmux, Kitty encode cache, half-block).
- Inside tmux, escapes need DCS passthrough and placements are renewed per frame; `TerminalCapabilities.InsideTmux` decides this and `Detect()` fills it from `TMUX`/`TERM`.

## Text width
- Column width comes from `TextUtils`, backed by a table generated from the Unicode Character Database (East_Asian_Width). CJK/emoji take two columns; combining marks take zero. Never use `string.Length` as a column count.
